findings.title: Delete cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. It does not invalidate or refetch trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, which is the query supplying cacheUpdatedAt to this component. After a successful cache deletion, the UI can continue showing the old cache status until some other refetch happens. The disconnect mutation already invalidates related queries; deleteCache should do the same.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the max updatedAt for all CalendarCache rows for a credential, without filtering expiresAt >= now(). Other cache-read paths ignore expired rows. This can make the UI display a cache status and delete action for expired/stale cache entries that would not actually be served.

findings.title: deleteCache authorization only allows directly owned credentials
findings.body: The handler checks credential ownership with { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }. Connected calendars can include delegation/team/service-account style credentials, and the UI explicitly handles delegationCredentialId. If a visible credential is not directly owned by the session user, the UI may show 'Delete cached data' but the mutation will fail. The authorization check should match the access model used to expose the credential, or the UI should hide the action when deletion is not permitted.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
findings.body: The script uses 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not present in dependencies or devDependencies. npx may download tsx on demand, causing nondeterministic versions, network dependence, and failures in offline or restricted environments. Add tsx as a devDependency or use the already available ts-node.

findings.title: Attempting to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt with an empty updateMany
findings.body: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is used to update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. An empty data object is fragile: depending on Prisma behavior it may be a no-op or may not reliably update @updatedAt for updateMany. If the intent is to touch records, pass an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires additional selected-calendar fields
findings.body: The exported UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars entries. This is a potentially breaking change for consumers of this exported/legacy type that construct or mock these objects, especially if they do not have these fields. If the fields are required by downstream code, this should be documented and call sites updated; otherwise consider keeping them optional.

findings.title: No automated tests for deleteCache authorization or cache status aggregation
findings.body: The PR introduces a destructive deleteCache mutation and a new cache-status aggregation method, but no unit/integration tests are included. Tests should cover at least: authorized deletion, rejection for another user's credential, correct getCacheStatusByCredentialIds behavior for multiple/expired cache rows, and connectedCalendars enrichment.

findings.title: Hardcoded en-US date format ignores user locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). This always renders US English formatting even when the user has another locale. Use the active app locale or the user's locale instead of hardcoding en-US.

findings.title: Credential lookup fetches full credential row unnecessarily
findings.body: prisma.credential.findFirst is called without a select, retrieving the entire credential record including encrypted secrets, only to check existence/ownership. Use select: { id: true } or select only the fields needed for authorization to avoid loading sensitive credential material into memory.

findings.title: Authorization failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: Throwing a plain Error for a missing or unauthorized credential produces a generic/internal tRPC error. Use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN so clients can distinguish authorization failures from unexpected server errors.

findings.title: connectedCalendars handler bypasses CalendarCache initialization/mock
findings.body: The handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly, while other cache read paths use CalendarCache.init(...), which can return a mock/no-op implementation when calendar-cache is disabled. If that gating is intentional, this handler can still expose DB-backed cache status even when calendar-cache functionality is disabled. Use the same factory or make the direct DB access intentional and documented.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts overly broad Prisma update type
findings.body: The method types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which can include relational nested updates. prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany only supports scalar/mutation update fields. Use Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput or a narrower type to prevent invalid callers from compiling or failing at runtime.

findings.title: Actions container renders even when dropdown is hidden
findings.body: The wrapper always renders <div className="flex w-32 justify-end"> around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for a delegation credential with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, this still reserves layout space and may misalign cards/alerts. Render the actions container only when an action is actually visible.

findings.body: The script uses sed -i '' -E, which fails on GNU/Linux because GNU sed treats '' as a backup suffix/file argument. If the script is intended to be cross-platform, use a portable in-place editing approach or detect the platform.
